routes.description: Establish that finite, composite beings exhibit real essence, form, and received existence, requiring an external self-existent ground that accounts for their unity, diversity, and actuality and can be identified with the God of classical theism.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if objective essences and essence-existence composition are established, the required ground is shown to be necessary and external to contingent reality, and the inference reaches classical theism rather than an unspecified cause.

motionBridge.description: Show that the necessary self-existent ground inferred from contingent composition possesses the identity required by the God of classical theism.

centralBridges.description: Establish that form or essence is an objective feature of beings and is not exhausted by physical description, classification, language, or assigned use.
Establish a real distinction in finite beings between what they are and the act by which they exist, requiring an account of their conjunction.
Show that the unity of diverse parts and the composition of essence with existence require an external composing ground rather than an unexplained natural arrangement.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Justify metaphysical reasoning about reality as a whole as an appropriate method for reaching conclusions unavailable from piecemeal empirical inquiry alone.
Specify how historical claims, reported miracles, prediction, explanatory scope, and personal experience could support identification of the necessary ground with a revealed God.

routes.description: Show that the proposed essence, composition, and necessary-ground claims lack independent demonstration and do not discriminate a divine agent from physical, descriptive, unknown, or non-agent explanations, leaving the classical-theist conclusion evidentially unwarranted.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the pro premises remain unsupported or adequately explained without additional metaphysical entities, the inference from grounding to agency or classical theism fails, and revelation or experience does not supply independently sufficient evidence.

motionBridge.description: Show that the presented considerations do not provide testable, independently supported, and discriminating evidence for the God of classical theism.

centralBridges.description: Require claims about God and metaphysical entities to receive support proportionate to their background plausibility and capable of distinguishing them from alternatives.
Account for identity, classification, form, and natural arrangement through physical properties, causal continuity, and human abstractions without positing independently existing essences.
Show that a need for explanation or causal grounding does not by itself establish intentional composition, a personal agent, or the God of classical theism.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Begin from observed beings and acknowledged uncertainty without classifying them as created or placing God among live explanations absent independent support.
Test claims of revelation and divine presence against sincere nonbelief, conflicting interpretation, and the apparent absence of clear universal disclosure.

sections.title: Metaphysical Method and Evidential Standards
sections.rationale: Determines whether reasoning about being as a whole can constitute good evidence and what independent support, testability, background knowledge, or explanatory discrimination the motion requires.

sections.title: Essence, Form, Identity, and Abstraction
sections.rationale: Addresses whether objective essences or forms exist beyond physical properties, causal continuity, classifications, linguistic concepts, intended functions, and changing material arrangements.

sections.title: Essence-Existence Composition and the Necessary Ground
sections.rationale: Covers the principal affirmative inference from finite beings whose essence and existence are distinct to a self-existent ground, together with objections to its premises and inferential validity.

sections.title: Composition, Causation, and the Inference to Agency
sections.rationale: Tests whether unity, diversity, parts, and observed effects require an external composer or personal cause, or whether that step assumes agency without discriminating evidence.

sections.title: From a Ground of Being to Classical Theism
sections.rationale: Examines whether the proposed necessary ground is adequately identified with the God of classical theism through philosophical identity claims, historical revelation, reported miracles, experience, and the challenge of divine hiddenness.

moves.speaker: Kenny Rhodes
moves.proposition: Metaphysical inquiry into reality as a whole can support conclusions about God that cannot be reached by empirically examining only isolated parts of reality.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator explicitly gives Rhodes the floor, and the uninterrupted opening statement remains his through this window.

response.rationale: This is a constructive methodological claim establishing the affirmative's proposed mode of metaphysical inquiry, so no earlier opposing move is targeted.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly states a method but supplies only a compressed defense of that method.

precisionFindings.rationale: The whole-versus-parts thesis is recoverable, but metaphysics, skepticism, and the limits of empirical inquiry are not sharply delimited.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The categorical claim that examining parts cannot answer whole-reality questions exceeds the methodological support supplied in the excerpt.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The inference assumes that empirical investigation of parts cannot support conclusions about wholes, leaving the central methodological bridge undefended.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The source offers an assertion about the limits of empirical inquiry and an authority reference, without representative evidence or rival comparison.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the subsidiary tier, the move directly supports the metaphysical-method bridge and is near the top of that range.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move advances its own methodological position without developing and evaluating a distinct live alternative.

moves.evidenceBasis: Rhodes says that isolating and examining parts cannot answer questions about God or the larger picture of reality.

moves.speaker: Kenny Rhodes
moves.proposition: The composite and multiple character of experienced reality requires an ultimate unified ground or existential absolute, which Rhodes identifies as God.
moves.attributionBasis: The claim occurs within Rhodes's continuous opening statement after his methodological discussion of metaphysics.

response.rationale: This constructive move supplies the affirmative composition principle and proposed unified ground, rather than responding to an earlier opposing move.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it states the intended inference clearly but compresses the decisive warrant from multiplicity to unity.

precisionFindings.rationale: The proposed inference is recoverable, but unity, ground, existential absolute, and multiplicity shift between descriptive and explanatory roles.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Necessity is asserted for the move from composite multiplicity to one ultimate ground without an adequate exclusion of alternative explanations.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The move repeatedly states that unity necessarily grounds multiplicity but does not establish why multiplicity requires one external ontological ground.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Its support consists chiefly of philosophical assertion and an appeal to Plato, with no defended warrant or comparison to natural alternatives.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly addresses the composing-ground requirement and is highly relevant to that indispensable step.

representationalCharity.rationale: No developed alternative account of multiplicity is considered within this constructive source span.

moves.evidenceBasis: Rhodes argues that composite reality and multiplicity necessarily lead back to one unified existential ground identified as God.

moves.speaker: Kenny Rhodes
moves.proposition: Classical monotheistic traditions converge on the uniquely possible simple reality whose essence is existence itself and which lies outside the category of finite beings.
moves.attributionBasis: Rhodes explicitly introduces a question he has heard Dillahunty ask and answers it during his uninterrupted opening.

response.rationale: This constructive move attempts the affirmative motion-level identification of the inferred simple ground with classical monotheism and has no reply target.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it expressly attempts the key identity bridge, though the cross-tradition convergence warrant remains compressed.

precisionFindings.rationale: The identity thesis is recoverable, but being outside being, existence itself, simplicity, and monotheistic identity are insufficiently distinguished.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The claim of a uniquely possible being shared across traditions is stronger than the brief definitional and historical assertions warrant.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Defining the ultimate as simple or as existence itself does not by itself establish uniqueness or identity across the named traditions.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The cross-tradition convergence and unique-possibility claims receive assertion rather than textual, historical, or independent philosophical support.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the motion tier, this directly attempts the indispensable identification of the ground with the God of classical theism.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move asserts convergence but does not engage a developed alternative interpretation requiring a charity test.

moves.evidenceBasis: Rhodes names Jewish, Christian, Islamic, and Greek traditions and describes their monotheistic referent as simple and existence itself.

moves.speaker: Kenny Rhodes
moves.proposition: Finite things exhibit a real distinction between what they are and their act of existence, whereas the ultimate ground must have essence and existence united.
moves.attributionBasis: This extended argument is delivered continuously by Rhodes and concludes immediately before he ends his opening statement.

response.rationale: This constructive move introduces the real essence-existence distinction central to the affirmative route, so it has no earlier opposing target.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it gives an intelligible example but leaves the transition from conceptual description to real composition underdeveloped.

precisionFindings.rationale: The finite-versus-self-existent contrast is recoverable, though essence and an act of existence are treated as components without full clarification.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The examples support a conceptual distinction more readily than the asserted real metaphysical composition and necessary ultimate contrast.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The unicorn example distinguishes conceivable essence from actuality, but the further claim of real metaphysical components remains a material bridge.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The move supplies illustrative cases, yet those examples do not independently establish that existence is an act composed with essence.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly advances the essence-existence composition bridge and is indispensable to the affirmative route.

representationalCharity.rationale: The constructive span does not expressly assess a competing account of predication, modality, or existential commitment.

moves.evidenceBasis: Rhodes contrasts definable unicorns and formerly existing dinosaurs to argue that what a thing is differs from its act of existence.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: Skepticism seeks to maximize true beliefs and minimize false ones through sound evidence and scientific inquiry, rather than rejecting claims merely because they are metaphysical.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator explicitly transfers the floor to Dillahunty, whose uninterrupted opening statement contains this first substantive rebuttal.

components.text: Whether skepticism and evidence-based inquiry are incapable of addressing metaphysical or whole-reality questions.

response.rationale: The reply directly rejects the portrayal of skepticism as mere metaphysical exclusion by defining it as truth-seeking through multiple evidential methods, including science.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it contacts the decisive methodological criticism but does not show how its methods answer whole-reality questions.

precisionFindings.rationale: The truth-seeking norm and inclusion of scientific inquiry among available methods are clearly and consistently stated.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The account of skepticism is well matched, though the claim that good-evidence problems are solved in science and courts is too broad.

charity.alternative: Rhodes may object to reductionist inquiry rather than to skepticism as such.
charity.decisiveQualification: Dillahunty defines his skepticism broadly but does not fully address whether piecemeal methods can reach metaphysical wholes.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The definition of skepticism and its truth-directed purpose are consistent, with only the link to resolving metaphysical questions left implicit.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Courtroom and scientific standards provide relevant examples, but the broad assertion that the evidential problem is solved is underdocumented.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the subsidiary tier, it directly attacks the affirmative methodological bridge and sits at the top of the tier.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply fairly corrects the broad characterization while leaving the strongest whole-versus-parts methodological concern incompletely answered.

moves.evidenceBasis: Dillahunty describes skepticism as maximizing true beliefs and minimizing false beliefs through scientific inquiry and good evidential standards.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: Claims require adequate justification, but familiar claims begin with substantial background evidence that unsupported claims about entities such as ghosts do not possess.
moves.attributionBasis: Dillahunty explicitly develops the extraordinary-claims maxim and contrasts mundane laundry claims with ghost reports.

response.rationale: This constructive move states an evidential standard based on prior background support and does not purport to answer one earlier locked move.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, the familiar-versus-extraordinary comparison clearly explains why equal immediate testimony can have unequal total support.

precisionFindings.rationale: The distinction between immediate evidence and accumulated background evidence is stated clearly with a bounded comparative scope.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The conclusion that background evidence affects reasonable acceptance is proportionate to the mundane-claim and ghost-claim comparison.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between evidential thresholds and differing prior support is explicit, consistent, and supported by a coherent comparison.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The examples substantiate the principle, though the move does not formalize priors or test the comparison against difficult borderline cases.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly establishes the con route's requirement for evidence proportionate to background plausibility.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move explains a general evidential principle without evaluating a developed opposing alternative in this span.

moves.evidenceBasis: Dillahunty contrasts familiar mundane claims, which inherit extensive background support, with unsupported reports such as ghosts.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: An unfalsifiable necessary-being conclusion is not good evidence when notions such as being and necessity are inserted without adequate justification or any possible test.
moves.attributionBasis: Dillahunty directly criticizes reasoning to a necessary being and then states his criteria for evidence in the same opening.

components.text: Whether the asserted essence-existence distinction and necessary being are adequately justified rather than inserted into the description.

response.rationale: The reply contacts the justification demand by challenging the insertion of necessity and being, although it does not separately analyze the unicorn-based distinction.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it reaches the decisive justificatory gap but offers limited engagement with the affirmative's specific metaphysical premises.

precisionFindings.rationale: The challenge is clear, but falsifiability is applied broadly without specifying which metaphysical propositions must admit empirical falsification.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The claim that an unsupported, untestable conclusion is not good evidence is proportionate, though falsifiability is treated somewhat expansively.

charity.alternative: A metaphysical claim may be rationally assessable through coherence and entailment without empirical falsifiability.
charity.decisiveQualification: Even on that interpretation, the premises introducing necessity and a necessary being still require an independent argument.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The criticism identifies a real missing-premise problem, though it partly conflates lack of empirical falsifiability with lack of rational warrant.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The excerpt accurately identifies unsupported inferential terms, but it supplies no detailed test of the affirmative essence-existence reasoning.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly attacks the essence-existence route and its transition to a necessary being.

representationalCharity.rationale: The objection preserves the possibility of argument while correctly pressing the missing justification for the necessity terminology.

moves.evidenceBasis: Dillahunty argues that being and necessity were injected without justification and that an unfalsifiable position does not supply good evidence.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: Observed existence and an asserted absolute ground do not themselves provide evidence for an agent, God, or the Trinity, and inquiry should not begin by presupposing those conclusions.
moves.attributionBasis: The turn explicitly contrasts the speaker's open-ended search for an explanation with Rhodes's God-directed approach.

components.text: Whether an asserted absolute or simple ground is thereby identified with an agent, God, the Trinity, or classical theism.
Whether the observed world supplies evidence for the proposed absolute ground rather than merely motivating an open explanatory question.

response.rationale: The reply expressly diagnoses the inference gap: observed reality and a demand for grounding do not discriminate an agent or Trinity, so the identity conclusion does not follow.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within diagnostic defeats, it explicitly identifies the missing ground-to-agent inference and states that inquiry should remain open absent evidence.

precisionFindings.rationale: The distinction between an unknown explanation, an absolute ground, an agent, God, and Trinity is clearly maintained.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The modest conclusion that the presented observations do not establish the specified agent matches the evidential gap identified.

charity.alternative: Rhodes may intend God as the metaphysical identity of the required simple ground, not as an additional empirical hypothesis.
charity.decisiveQualification: That identity still requires premises showing agency and classical-theist attributes rather than an unspecified ground.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between needing an explanation and having evidence for a particular agent is explicit and defeats the unsupported identity inference.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The warrant rests appropriately on the affirmative's missing discriminating evidence, though it does not canvass every philosophical identity argument.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the motion tier, it directly attacks the indispensable bridge from a proposed ground to the God of classical theism.

representationalCharity.rationale: The response grants the search for explanation while accurately isolating the unestablished identification with agentive classical theism.

moves.evidenceBasis: Dillahunty says the observed world does not evidence a Trinity, God, being, required ground, or any agent and warns against presupposition.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: The burnt-wood inference is supported by repeated empirical evidence for fire, whereas no comparable evidence establishes essence, existence itself, or a required metaphysical ground.
moves.attributionBasis: Dillahunty directly rejects Rhodes's analogy and identifies the missing independent evidence for its metaphysical counterpart.

components.text: Whether ordinary explanatory analogies provide independent support for essence, an act of existence, and a necessary metaphysical ground.

response.rationale: The reply identifies the defeating disanalogy: fire is independently and repeatedly observed, while essence and existence-as-entities lack comparable support, so the analogy cannot carry the conclusion.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within diagnostic defeats, it explicitly names the evidential feature that supports the mundane inference and is absent from the metaphysical analogue.

precisionFindings.rationale: The empirical-evidence contrast and its limited consequence for the proposed analogy are clearly and consistently expressed.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The conclusion is limited to the analogy's failure to establish its metaphysical counterpart and fits the stated disanalogy.

charity.alternative: The burnt-wood example may illustrate abductive form rather than claim equal empirical support for metaphysical entities.
charity.decisiveQualification: An analogous inferential form still needs independent grounds for the relevant metaphysical premises and comparison class.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The response cleanly distinguishes shared inferential form from the independent evidence that makes the fire explanation credible.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Repeated observation of burning directly supports the stated contrast, with only the broader theory of metaphysical evidence left undeveloped.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly attacks the evidential warrant for the essence-existence composition inference.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply considers the strongest illustrative reading and accurately preserves the demand for independent support of the metaphysical premises.

moves.evidenceBasis: Dillahunty contrasts extensive observation of fire and burned wood with the absence of comparable evidence for essence or existence itself.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: Human nature and similar general notions package descriptions of physical beings and their behavior rather than naming independently existing essences.
moves.attributionBasis: The speaker expressly denies an additional human essence and explains nature, spirit, and number language as descriptive abstraction.

components.text: Whether general terms such as human nature designate real essences rather than abstractions packaging physical beings and behavior.

response.rationale: The reply directly offers a descriptive-abstraction account of nature terms, contacting the ontological premise but not the separate essence-existence argument in full.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it contacts the decisive objective-essence premise and supplies an alternative account, though continuity is not yet addressed.

precisionFindings.rationale: The distinction between existing beings and abstract descriptions of their behavior is clear, with only the nominalist scope left implicit.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The examples support an abstraction account, but they do not conclusively exclude every realist account of common natures.

charity.alternative: A realist may hold that nature is instantiated in individuals rather than existing as a separate object.
charity.decisiveQualification: The abstraction examples alone do not decide whether shared structural features are merely described or objectively instantiated.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The separation of concrete entities and abstract descriptions is coherent, though it does not entail that no objective common structure exists.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The behavior and number examples illustrate abstraction well but leave the decisive nominalism-versus-realism warrant compressed.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly supports the descriptive-ontology bridge regarding nature, classification, and abstraction.

representationalCharity.rationale: The response gives a plausible nominalist account but does not fully address the strongest immanent-realist interpretation of essence.

moves.evidenceBasis: Dillahunty says human nature packages descriptions of beings and behavior, comparing this abstraction to representations of the number two.

moves.speaker: Kenny Rhodes
moves.proposition: Human continuity through ongoing material change requires a persisting form or essence; otherwise a person would become wholly different at every moment.
moves.attributionBasis: Rhodes invokes total material replacement, the Ship of Theseus, and responsibility over time to argue for essential continuity.

components.text: Whether a purely descriptive account can explain personal identity and responsibility through ongoing material and temporal change.

response.rationale: The reply contacts the abstraction account by pressing diachronic identity and responsibility, but it does not establish that an immaterial or metaphysical form is the only solution.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it reaches a decisive continuity challenge but leaves the inference from persistence to objective essence incomplete.

precisionFindings.rationale: The continuity challenge is recoverable, but form, essence, definition, and personal identity are not adequately distinguished.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Persistence raises an explanatory problem, but it does not by itself necessitate a metaphysical form rather than causal or psychological continuity.

charity.alternative: A descriptive physicalist can ground identity in causal, biological, psychological, or conventional continuity despite material change.
charity.decisiveQualification: Material replacement alone does not show that those continuity relations fail or that a separate form is required.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The move exposes a persistence question but advances a false dilemma between momentary total difference and a persisting metaphysical form.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Material change and responsibility are relevant examples, yet they do not independently establish the proposed ontological essence.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly attacks the descriptive-ontology account by challenging its treatment of diachronic identity.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move identifies a serious identity question but omits the strongest continuity-based physicalist response and overstates the forced choice.

moves.evidenceBasis: Rhodes invokes material replacement, the Ship of Theseus, and responsibility over time to argue that some persisting form is required.

moves.speaker: Kenny Rhodes
moves.proposition: Although labels and definitions are conventional, they signify an objective reality whose nature or essence is not created by the chosen language.
moves.attributionBasis: Rhodes resumes after the moderator's clarification and distinguishes arbitrary words from the realities those words signify.

components.text: Whether conventional definitions merely create classifications or instead describe an objective nature belonging to the thing.

response.rationale: The reply directly distinguishes conventional words from objective referents, contacting the abstraction thesis, but it asserts rather than demonstrates the further essence claim.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it contacts the decisive language-versus-reality issue while leaving the objective-essence inference substantially compressed.

precisionFindings.rationale: The word-referent distinction is clear, though nature, essence, reality, and definition remain partly interchangeable.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Conventional labels plainly can refer to objective things, but that does not alone establish objective essences in the stronger metaphysical sense.

charity.alternative: The con position can accept objective physical referents while treating their classifications and common natures as conceptual abstractions.
charity.decisiveQualification: Mind-independent objects do not by themselves entail mind-independent essences corresponding to every useful definition.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The referent distinction is valid, but the conclusion that the referent therefore has an objective metaphysical essence requires another premise.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The linguistic distinction supplies relevant conceptual support but no independent evidence deciding realism about natures.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly attacks the con descriptive-ontology bridge at the language and classification step.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply fairly distinguishes words from things but does not fully engage the stronger nominalist account of objective referents and conventional kinds.

moves.evidenceBasis: Rhodes agrees that definitions and labels are chosen while insisting that they describe a reality whose nature is not created by language.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: A pen can be identified through physical properties, function, and shared learned concepts without establishing any additional nonphysical essence.
moves.attributionBasis: Dillahunty develops the pen example and explains recognition through shared language and similar mental concepts.

components.text: Whether identifying and describing an object requires an additional nonphysical essence beyond physical properties, function, and learned concepts.
Whether the pen example answers the separate problem of diachronic personal persistence through material change.

response.rationale: The reply directly challenges the claimed extra essence through exhaustive physical description and shared concepts, but it does not answer the distinct persistence argument.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it contacts the principal objective-nature claim while leaving the earlier continuity-based demand uncontacted.

precisionFindings.rationale: The claim is carefully limited to what the pen example establishes about description, function, concepts, and alleged nonphysical essence.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The request for the alleged nonphysical remainder is appropriately calibrated as a challenge rather than a conclusive proof of nominalism.

charity.alternative: An artifact essence may be functional or structurally instantiated rather than a separable nonphysical property.
charity.decisiveQualification: Physical and functional description can identify the pen without settling whether those organized features instantiate an objective kind.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The challenge coherently shows that successful identification does not visibly require an additional nonphysical property.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The detailed inventory of observable properties and learned concepts supports the claim, with ontology beyond the example remaining open.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly attacks the objective-essence bridge through the pen classification case.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply fairly presses the need for an additional property while leaving room for an immanent structural interpretation.

moves.evidenceBasis: Dillahunty lists the pen's physical properties and explains recognition through shared language, function, and similar learned mental concepts.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: Known artifacts warrant an inference to intentional assembly because their design and manufacture are independently established, but humans and natural objects lack corresponding evidence of assembly by an agent.
moves.attributionBasis: Dillahunty gives an extended contrast between documented artifact manufacture and unsupported inferences about natural entities.

components.text: Whether composition or multiplicity itself licenses an inference to intentional assembly or an external composing agent.

response.rationale: The reply diagnoses that artifact inferences depend on independent knowledge of design and manufacture, which is missing for humans and natural objects, defeating the analogy to agency.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within diagnostic defeats, it expressly identifies the evidential difference and states why the inference cannot transfer to natural composition.

precisionFindings.rationale: Artifact, design, manufacture, natural object, and agent are consistently distinguished with a clear comparative scope.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The limited conclusion that the artifact inference lacks an established natural analogue fits the independent-evidence contrast.

charity.alternative: The affirmative may invoke a universal metaphysical composition principle rather than an empirical artifact analogy.
charity.decisiveQualification: That universal principle still requires independent justification and cannot borrow the evidential warrant specific to known manufacture.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The response clearly separates known intentional manufacture from bare composition and blocks the transfer without assuming naturalism.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Independent knowledge of how artifacts are designed and built provides specific representative support for the stated disanalogy.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly supports the agency-gap bridge and reaches the top of that relevance range.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply handles the strongest nonanalogical reading by isolating the same missing warrant for agency beyond mere composition.

moves.evidenceBasis: Dillahunty notes that car design and manufacture are independently known, while no comparable record shows humans or natural objects were assembled by agents.

moves.speaker: Kenny Rhodes
moves.proposition: The universe unifies diverse constituents such as time, space, matter, and energy, and this composition requires an external composing ground or agent.
moves.attributionBasis: Rhodes responds to the artifact comparison by extending the composition principle to reality as a whole.

components.text: Whether the universe's composition supplies a general basis for inferring an external composer despite the artifact-natural disanalogy.

response.rationale: The reply contacts the disanalogy by asserting a universal composition principle, but calling it self-evident does not supply the independent warrant the objection requested.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it addresses the decisive agency issue but largely restates the disputed inference rather than defending it.

precisionFindings.rationale: Ground, something, someone, put together, composed, and agent are used across causal and intentional senses without stable separation.

calibrationFindings.rationale: A necessary external agent is asserted as nearly self-evident from listed constituents despite the immediately identified natural-artifact warrant gap.

charity.alternative: Composition might require some explanatory condition without requiring intentional assembly by a personal agent.
charity.decisiveQualification: The move shifts from something to someone and put together without excluding non-agent causal or structural explanations.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The move equivocates between causal ground and intentional composer, and its universal agent premise substantially assumes the disputed conclusion.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Listing time, space, matter, and energy supplies no independent evidence that these were intentionally assembled by an external agent.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly attacks the con agency-gap bridge even though its attempted warrant is seriously defective.

representationalCharity.rationale: The response acknowledges a ground in broad terms but materially weakens the non-agent alternative by treating composition as intentional assembly.

moves.evidenceBasis: Rhodes lists time, space, matter, and energy as universe parts and infers that something or someone must have put them together.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: Assuming that every parts-bearing entity was assembled by an agent makes the composition argument circular and leaves the existence of an intentional composer undemonstrated.
moves.attributionBasis: Dillahunty immediately identifies the universal-agent premise as the conclusion under dispute and separates explanation from agency.

components.text: Whether composition independently establishes an intentional composer rather than presupposing that all parts-bearing things are agent-assembled.

response.rationale: The reply expressly identifies the premise as the disputed conclusion and states the defeating consequence: the argument assumes an agent instead of demonstrating one.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within diagnostic defeats, it precisely contacts the decisive universal-agent premise and explains why the resulting argument is circular.

precisionFindings.rationale: The challenged premise, circular structure, intentional composer, and limited defeating consequence are all clearly recoverable.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Given the stated premise that every composition requires an agent, identifying question-begging in the immediate inference is proportionate.

charity.alternative: The affirmative might mean that every contingent composition requires a cause, not necessarily a personal agent.
charity.decisiveQualification: The actual move expressly advances from composed parts to someone who put them together, so agency remains embedded in the premise.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The reply accurately exposes that the universal agent premise contains the conclusion and separates generic explanation from intentional agency.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The immediately preceding formulation supplies direct textual support for the circularity diagnosis; no external factual premise is needed.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly supports the agency-gap bridge against the affirmative's explicit composer inference.

representationalCharity.rationale: The objection distinguishes a generic explanatory cause from the explicitly intentional conclusion and targets only the latter's circular support.

moves.evidenceBasis: Dillahunty says the claim excludes any non-agent composition by assumption and therefore presupposes the God-composer it seeks to demonstrate.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: A sincere nonbeliever would accept a clearly revealed God, while God's apparent failure to provide unmistakable universal disclosure supports a divine-hiddenness objection.
moves.attributionBasis: Dillahunty answers a direct question about discovering God and develops the implications of God's apparent failure to reveal itself.

response.rationale: This is a constructive hiddenness objection based on sincere openness and the apparent absence of unmistakable universal disclosure, so it has no reply target.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly states the experiential tension but does not develop expected-disclosure conditions or competing explanations.

precisionFindings.rationale: The sincere-nonbelief thesis is clear, but clearly reveal and all of us without question set a broad disclosure standard without full qualification.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The speaker frames hiddenness as something he does not understand and as a reason for doubt, fitting the personal evidential basis.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Sincere willingness to believe and apparent non-disclosure create a coherent evidential tension, though the expected-revelation premise remains implicit.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The move supplies relevant first-person evidence of openness but does not establish representativeness or compare divine reasons for permitting ambiguity.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the subsidiary tier, it directly supports the hiddenness-check bridge and sits at the top of that range.

representationalCharity.rationale: The constructive span does not develop a specific theistic explanation of hiddenness sufficiently to test it.

moves.evidenceBasis: Dillahunty says he would believe a clearly revealed God and questions why such a God does not disclose itself unmistakably to everyone.

moves.speaker: Kenny Rhodes
moves.proposition: Because finite beings possess existence accidentally rather than in themselves, their existence logically entails a per-se or self-existent ground.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator directs the question to Rhodes, and the uninterrupted answer continues until the moderator closes the turn.

components.text: Whether the transition from finite or accidental existence to a per-se self-existent ground has an articulated logical principle.
Whether a self-declared metaphysical principle supplies the independent evidential warrant missing from the burnt-wood analogy.

response.rationale: The reply supplies the per-accidens-to-per-se principle as an answer to the missing-bridge challenge, but it does not defend applying that principle to existence itself.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it contacts the decisive missing inference but leaves both the category application and independent warrant unresolved.

precisionFindings.rationale: The intended principle is recoverable, but accidental shifts from inhering property to dependent possession of existence, obscuring its scope.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Calling the principle self-evident and undeniable overstates what the tallness analogy establishes about existence and a self-existent ground.

charity.alternative: Finite beings may exist dependently without existence being an accident inhering in a self-existent substance.
charity.decisiveQualification: The tallness analogy does not show that existence is the same kind of accidental predicate or that one per-se bearer follows.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The inference equivocates between ordinary accidents inhering in substances and finite beings' alleged accidental possession of existence.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The tallness analogy illustrates per-accidens predication but does not independently warrant a unique self-existent ontological ground.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly advances the essence-existence composition bridge and answers a central justificatory challenge.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply presents a recognizable scholastic principle but does not engage the strongest challenge to its application to existence.

moves.evidenceBasis: Rhodes invokes the scholastic principle that per accidens implies per se, analogizing accidental existence to tallness inhering in a substance.

moves.speaker: Kenny Rhodes
moves.proposition: A claimed divine revelation can be assessed through historical documents, miracle reports, fulfilled prediction, and explanatory scope concerning origin, meaning, morality, and destiny.
moves.attributionBasis: Dillahunty asks Rhodes how revelation could be recognized, and Rhodes gives the complete answer before the moderator moves to another question.

components.text: Whether purported divine revelation has publicly assessable indicators beyond private conviction or ambiguous personal experience.
Whether historical revelation could provide the additional evidence needed to identify an abstract ground with a revealed God.

response.rationale: The reply specifies public historical and explanatory tests for revelation, contacting both evidential accessibility and identification, though it supplies no test results.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it gives relevant verification criteria but does not answer why clear disclosure remains absent or show that any revelation passes.

precisionFindings.rationale: The move clearly presents historical documents, prediction, miracles, and explanatory scope as proposed tests rather than established successes.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The modest claim that revelation can be assessed by these criteria is appropriately distinguished from claiming that Christianity has passed them.

charity.alternative: Historical texts and reported predictions may remain ambiguous, dependent, or compatible with nondivine explanations.
charity.decisiveQualification: The move proposes tests but does not yet establish independence, authenticity, fulfilled prediction, or divine discrimination.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The proposed sequence from treating texts historically to evaluating predictions and explanatory scope is coherent and appropriately conditional.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The move names potentially relevant evidence but supplies no documents, miracle verification, fulfilled predictions, or comparison with rival explanations.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the subsidiary tier, it directly supports the revelation-and-experience bridge and reaches the top of that range.

representationalCharity.rationale: The answer fairly treats revelation as assessable evidence while leaving the skeptical verification and alternative-explanation demands open.

moves.evidenceBasis: Rhodes proposes treating biblical materials as historical documents and testing prophecy, miracles, and explanatory scope before attributing divine inspiration.

moves.speaker: Kenny Rhodes
moves.proposition: The inference from a necessary creator to the Christian God is philosophical rather than empirical because piecemeal examination of parts cannot resolve the nature of reality as a whole.
moves.attributionBasis: The question is explicitly addressed to Rhodes, and the short first-person answer ends before he shifts to explaining his physical condition.

components.text: Whether the inference to the Christian God has adequate independently supported and discriminating evidence given its background plausibility.
Whether philosophical reasoning supplies the missing identity bridge from necessary creator to the specifically Christian God.
Whether empirical examination of parts is methodologically sufficient for questions about reality as a whole.

response.rationale: The reply reiterates a methodological limit on empirical inquiry, but it neither supplies the requested identity argument nor addresses background support and discrimination for Christianity.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within relevant nonanswers, the whole-versus-parts point bears on method but leaves the decisive evidential and identification demands uncontacted.

precisionFindings.rationale: The short answer contrasts empirical parts with reality as a whole, but the claimed inference to Christian identity is not actually articulated.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The categorical denial that empirical evidence can be given does not establish that the proposed philosophical route reaches Christianity.

charity.alternative: The evidential challenge allows philosophical evidence if it independently supports and discriminates the Christian conclusion.
charity.decisiveQualification: Labeling the inference philosophical does not answer whether its premises identify Christianity rather than another ground or explanation.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The answer does not contain a usable inference from empirical limitation to a necessary creator, still less to the Christian God.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: No philosophical premises, historical facts, or discriminating evidence are supplied in this short span for the specifically Christian conclusion.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it attacks the con evidential standard by denying empirical applicability, though only at the lower end.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply narrows the opponent to piecemeal empiricism and omits the stronger demand for any independently warranted discriminating argument.

moves.evidenceBasis: Rhodes says he cannot give empirical evidence because examining reality part by part cannot explain the nature of the whole.
